> Aussiefied at **Swaggie** level, with **Dinkum** embellishment and **Dad** vulgarity. [Prefer docs that are as dry as a dead dingo's donger?](../plain/functional/dictionary.md)

# The dictionary

All the slang is data: every phrase is an entry in the YAML dictionary under `aussiefy/data/`, and every level is
a profile in `aussiefy/data/profiles.yaml` (see
[DD-002](../architecture/decisions/dd-002-slang-is-data.md)). Jeez Louise, this page describes the files, the entry format
and the checks the loader runs. Well, how entries get into the dictionary is in the contributor guide to
[data acquisition](../contributor/data-acquisition.md).

## Files

```
aussiefy/data/
  concepts.yaml        controlled concept vocabulary + plain-English trigger patterns per frame
  grammar.yaml         editable person nouns, adjective/noun sense limits and reviewed name-comparison aliases for the frame checker
  profiles.yaml        level profiles 1-5, the swearing rates per vulgarity, and policy defaults
  phonetic.yaml        drawl: contractions (level 4+), respellings (level 5), swear infixes (by vulgarity),
                       and Australian spelling (kind: spelling)
                       optional unless_before regex excludes grammatical contexts before a rule match
                       optional unless_question boolean excludes matches in question sentences
  riffs.yaml           the image a term calls up (wheelie bin: bin chickens fightin' over the scraps)
  imagery.yaml         reviewed contextual images, meaning/frame anchors and writer usage conditions
  guide.yaml           voice, language limits, openings, gated craft, workflow, plan note and yarn rules
  swears.yaml          swear words by strength, for lint and for rating riffs
  dialect.yaml         US/UK patterns, Australian replacements, sense guards and lint-only expressions
  genres.yaml          explicit document presets and embellishment settings
  judge.yaml           blind comparison rubric and report schema
  pos/                 licensed English POS weights and provenance metadata
  source_policy.yaml   sites the scraper must not bulk-extract (reference-only)
  sources.yaml         extra source URLs per entry (written by `dev review --apply`)
  model/               the bundled static embedding model
  entries/
    lexical.yaml       one-word swaps: nouns, adjectives, adverbs
    phrases.yaml       interjections, imperatives, short noun phrases
    idioms.yaml        predicate / verb-phrase / clause idioms
    garnish.yaml       connectives, openers, tag-ons, asides, tails, closers
    swearing.yaml      plain-word swears (fuckin', fuck all, a dickhead, no bastard, some cunt)
    fragments.yaml     slang found inside existing idioms
    gapfill.yaml       the gap-fill research round (research/gap-fill-2026-10-11)
    classics.yaml      the classics research round (research/classics-2026-10-11)
    meaning-extensions.yaml  reviewed sense splits and explicitly requested vocabulary
    flagged.yaml       omitted and gated entries (kept so re-scrapes don't reintroduce them)
    scraped.yaml       machine-managed output of the review tool
```

## Entries

An entry is one meaning\-shape:

```yaml
- id: roos-top-paddock
  form: "{subj} {have} a kangaroo loose in {poss} top paddock"
  variants: ["{subj} {have} kangaroos loose in {poss} top paddock"]
  concept: [CRAZY]
  frame: clause          # predicate_adj | np | adj | adv | vp | clause | interjection | imperative | tag
  intensity: 4           # 1-5
  vulgarity: 0           # 0 clean, 1 mild (bloody, bastard), 2 impolite (piss, arse, fuck), 3 the c-word
  incoherence: 4         # minimum level at which the entry is eligible
  register: current      # current | dated | archaic
  region: []             # e.g. [qld]
  replaces: []           # plain-English paraphrases (patterns); drive matching
  status: active         # active | gate | omit
  flags: []              # not_aussie | slur | dubious_meaning | archaic | fabricated | untagged
  semantic_effects: []   # reviewed additions to the mapped meaning; opinion or quantity_approximation
  sources: []
  gloss: Not quite sane; eccentric.   # our own words, never a source's
```

An entry's `incoherence` (its minimum level\) says how hard it is to follow, never how rude it is; rudeness is
its `vulgarity`. A `gate` entry is held back until all its flags are unlocked \(`--unlock`, or `--unlock all`); an
`omit` entry is never used, and is kept only so that re\-scrapes recognise it.

`riffs.yaml` maps entry IDs to optional images, each with `text` and `tone` (`comic`, `grim` or `plain`).
Anyway, these can include original comparisons as well as familiar imagery; they aren't additional meanings or
automatically attested sayings. Lookup offers only riffs within the swear cap, with the first eligible one
marked `best`. Plans apply the effective document/embellishment permissions; translations additionally apply
profile probabilities, spacin''n limits. No extra persona setting is required to use a harvested riff.

Further optional fields:

- `slots` are inferred from the placeholders in `form`.
- `plural` handles irregular noun plurals.
- `class` (lexical, phrase or idiom\) overrides how the level profile treats an entry.
- `weight` sets an entry's prior.
- `notes` holds review notes.
- `key_sha256` lets an omitted entry (for example a slur) block re-scrapes without storing the text.
- `mask` lists the profane words a page may hide in the entry's renderings, at its vulgarity, where they aren't
  on the swear list \(`mask: [wanker]`). Each must be a lower\-case word in one of its forms. They stay outta
  `swears.yaml` 'cause lint reads that list.
- `profane: false` marks an entry rated 1 or more with no profanity in it: innuendo \("rooted", "have a root"\), an
  insult \("mongrel"\) or a crude word \("shut your gob"\). Not a sausage in it's masked. So anyway, a test fails when an active entry
  rated 1 or more has neither a masked word at its rating nor this mark \([changes](changes.md#masks)).
- `type: garnish` entries carry `placement` (connective, opener, tag, aside, tail or closer\), an optional
  `when` (the sentence contexts they suit\) and an optional `stretch` (vowel\-stretch the closer, as in
  "Faaaaaark me").

## Sense boundaries

Keep distinct meanings in distinct concepts. A `lout` isn't necessarily a `reckless driver`, and an
`itinerant worker` isn't necessarily a `vagrant`; `comradeship` is narrower than `devotion`. An entry may serve several
concepts, but its direct `replaces` patterns then introduce all of those concepts: prefer the individual
concept triggers when those meanings need different candidates.

Now, named cultural references such as `Goon of Fortune` and `Hills Hoist` are retained with specific meanings;
they don't turn every drinkin' game or rotary clothesline into the named game or brand. Look, appetite phrases
such as “could do with a feed” and “wouldn't say no to some tucker” have direct mappings for corresponding
conditional requests, plus writer\-only hunger suggestions for contexts requirin' tense or modal judgement.

A concept may declare `lookup_only: true` to retain writer discovery while excluding automatic triggers
and direct entry replacements for that meaning. This is an actual boolean, independent of entry status,
register and flags. A mixed entry can still serve its other automatic meanings. Source forms remain in
the recognition index. Intentional discovery-only concepts do not generate unreachable-trigger warnings.

## Slots

Slots are `{subj} {be} {have} {do} {poss} {obj} {objposs}`, plus `{np}`, which captures a short noun phrase'n copies
it across, and `{will}`, which becomes "will" or "would" by tense. For example, `reckon {np} {have} Buckley's`
turns "believing her assertion to be simply impossible" into "reckoning her assertion had Buckley's". When an
entry has no verb of its own to take tense from, it uses the rest of the sentence's tense. Stone the flamin' crows, clause forms can
also start with "there" ("it's impossible" → "there's no bloody way").

`{objposs}` identifies another participant's possessive. It uses an explicit captured possessive or
derives one from `{obj}`; it never falls back to the speaking agent. Bloody hell, for example, “she talked his ear
off” can become “she bent his ear”, while bare “she rambled” supplies no listener. Selected forms must
retain an explicitly captured object possessive, just as they retain other captured arguments.

`number: mass` marks an uncountable noun, overriding spelling heuristics for forms such as `kid stakes`.
Crikey, mass terms are withheld for explicitly plural source spans'n counted noun phrases outside the match
(such as `one warm beer`, `another beer` or `each beer`). Mass\-compatible quantifiers such as `some`,
`much` and `no` remain valid; the engine doesn't rewrite surrounding agreement to force a term in. `number: plural` retains
its existin' plural\-only referent meanin', and omitted number metadata remains `any`.

## Pattern language

`replaces` and concept triggers share a small pattern language:

- literals, and `{slot}`
- `a|an` alternatives
- `word?` for an optional word
- `!war|deal` to block a sense: neither of the next two words may be one of these, so `great !war` skips "a
  great civil war" but still fires on "a great game"
- `?=home|there` requires the next token without consumin' it: `walk ?=home|there` preserves the destination
- `?<=radio|car antenna` requires a precedin' token without consuming it: replace the antenna head while
  retaining its wireless/car qualifier. Assertion alternatives each name one token. Fair dinkum, following assertions
  require a precedin' consuming element; matchin' still enforces both assertions in similarity mode
- `^object` requires an `{np}` argument'n applies shared unanchored\-object checks, rejecting temporal
  and quantity\-only adjuncts rather than mistaking them for the object of a multiword expression
- `^person` limits a predicate to a person; `^adj` requires a following modifier
- `^end` on a verb phrase or clause requires a clause boundary after optional adverbial tails, preservin' complements
  such as the habit in “quit smoking”; it isn't supported on other frames
- a trailin' `@N` for intensity

In `vp` patterns the head verb matches any inflection, and in `np` patterns the head noun matches its plural,
including accepted alternative spellings such as antennas/antennae. Assertions don't become head words
or enter a lookup/trainin' phrase as translated content.

## Validation

Now, the loader validates whole box'n dice at load time: field types and ranges, kebab\-case ids, known concepts and
slots, clause forms starting with `{subj}`, `slur` forcing `omit`, no duplicate ids, and that every form
compiles as a pattern. It collects every error, with file'n id, and raises one `SchemaError` (the CLI exits
2\). It also warns about concepts that can never be detected'n flagged entries left active.
`aussiefy validate` runs the same checks'n prints stats. Required concepts, profiles, phonetic, swears,
genre, riffs'n entries files must be present; malformed YAML and missing files are collected
with the other errors. String\-list fields require strings, `person` and `stretch` require real booleans,
and profile garnish keys must name known placements. Mate, the guide validates its own structure'n dial keys.

## Extending it

To extend the dictionary without touching the package, pass `--dict my-entries.yaml` (a file or a directory;
repeatable) to any command, or `load_dictionary(["my-entries.yaml"])` in Python. A step-by-step guide is in
[getting-started.md](../user/getting-started.md#add-your-own-entries).

### Dictionary overlays

Anyway, an ordinary entry\-list file remains addition\-only: duplicate IDs are errors. A versioned overlay uses the
same `--dict` option to add or patch vocabulary records explicitly. This changes the dictionary compiled
for that translator; it doesn't replace strings in rendered output or bypass meaning, grammar or dial checks.

```yaml
format: aussiefy-dictionary-overlay/v1
patch_entries:
  brave-bastards:
    concept: [BRAVE]
    replaces: []
```

Mate, this example records the current bravery\-only mapping'n clears any entry\-specific direct triggers. It
doesn't make every digger brave. A faulty shared concept trigger must also be corrected in that concept's
`triggers` field; adding a better candidate alone doesn't disable the old mapping.

The optional sections are `add_concepts` (a map of new IDs to concept records), `add_entries` (an entry list),
`patch_concepts` and `patch_entries` (maps of existing IDs to changed fields). Additions reject existing IDs;
patches require a target already present and cannot rename its ID. New records use the ordinary schemas.
An overlay may add a narrower meaning and move an existing entry to it, with reusable patterns and slots.

Composition order is built\-in records with their source sidecar, then `--dict` arguments in command order.
Well, a directory expands nonrecursively: sorted `*.yaml` files, followed by sorted `*.yml` files, preservin' the
existin' custom\-dictionary order. Within an overlay, add concepts, add entries, patch concepts, then patch
entries. Cross\-record references resolve against the final dictionary before its indexes are built once.

Omitted fields inherit. Supplied fields replace the entire field: `variants: []` clears variants,
`replaces: []` clears direct triggers, and `triggers: {}` clears a concept's triggers. So anyway, a supplied `triggers`
map replaces all its old frames; it doesn't append to them. Later files win for fields they explicitly set.
Invalid operations remain errors even if a later file would overwrite them. Unknown keys, formats, targets
and duplicate explicit YAML keys are errors. Standard YAML anchors'n merge keys remain supported.
Normal schema validation applies to every operation'n the final data.

Sources inherit unless explicitly replaced. `sources: []` clears inline and sidecar references for that entry;
the bundled sidecar is not reapplied afterward. When changing a meaning or form, review whether inherited
sources still support it. Overlay origin identifies the correction file, not evidence that a term is attested.
Entries first introduced by extra files inherit applicable sidecar references when they are added, before
patch operations. This also preserves source inheritance when loading a custom entry inventory with
`include_builtin=False`; an explicit source patch still wins.
`aussiefy validate --dict corrections.yaml` reports operations, `show` adds origin comments, and Python callers
can inspect `dictionary.overlay_changes` and an entry's effective `origin_file`.

V1 overlays cover entries'n concepts. Riffs, imagery, grammar, dial presets and other auxiliary files keep
their existin' formats; this isn't a general patch format for every package file. Load failures change no
shipped files, and separate translators retain independent dictionaries.

Behaviour overrides in `document_config` are separate: they choose which engine behaviours a run permits.
Dictionary overlays provide vocabulary knowledge; behaviour settings control its use. Corpus tests and
the research/review tools should drive corrections. Shared grammar defects belong in the engine with
positive and negative regressions, rather than an accumulating list of phrase-specific exceptions.

## Reviewed semantic additions

`semantic_effects: [opinion]` declares that every meaning mapping and form of an entry adds narrator judgment
beyond its input meaning. The default empty list adds no declared effect; the loader rejects unknown effects.
The ALIVE mapping for "the lucky buggers still breathin'" adds a judgment of good fortune and requires the
resolved `narrator_opinion` permission. The ordinary meaning, grammar, vulgarity and tone checks still apply.
Annotated garnish extensions use the same permission and are included in the existing form index for known-term writer checks.

Annotation is about a mapping, not the mere presence of evaluative words. A synonym for GOOD_PERSON can carry
praise already established by its input without requiring an added-opinion annotation. Do not combine an
exact and an opinion-adding sense in one entry under the same metadata. These reviewed annotations cover
specific entries; they are not an audit or automatic interpretation of every dictionary mapping.

### Source-specific additions

Entry `semantic_effects` applies to every mapping and form of an entry. Where only one source-to-concept
mapping loses information, annotate the exact raw trigger instead:

```yaml
LONG_AGO:
  description: An indefinite distant time.
  triggers:
    adv: ["ages ago", "four score and seven years ago@5"]
  trigger_effects:
    adv:
      "four score and seven years ago@5": [quantity_approximation]
```

Frame'n pattern keys must already exist, including their `@N` suffix; effect names use the same vocabulary
as entries. Effects remain concept\-scoped. Exact direct replacements for the same span can't bypass the
reviewed source annotation, while a separate precise readin' doesn't inherit another meanin''s effect.
Research\-round style rewrites retain annotations under their rewritten trigger keys. Replacing triggers
through an overlay must also keep or replace their annotation maps coherently.

Plans, explanations'n change alternatives expose effects of the applied mapping. A bare term such as
“yonks ago” isn't inherently lossy. Meaning lookup respects source annotations in contextual queries,
while explicit term discovery remains available. Lint/verify require an original to check these mappings:
they recognise unambiguous local edits connecting reviewed source spans to compatible dictionary forms.
Ambiguous edits'n arbitrary paraphrases are outside that check. Allowed quantity mappings excuse only
numbers inside their paired source occurrence; other missing numbers retain fidelity warnings.

## Reviewed semantic degree

`semantic_degree: {DRUNK: strong}` certifies an entry's degree for a mapped concept. Allowed bands are
`mild`, `unmarked` and `strong`; omitted metadata means unknown, not an assumed middle grade. A certificate
covers every form of that entry. Split forms with different degrees into separate entries, as with
`a bit full` and bare `full`. The map's keys must belong to the entry's concepts.

Concepts certify source wording separately, by exact frame'n raw trigger including any `@N` suffix:

```yaml
trigger_degrees:
  predicate_adj:
    drunk: unmarked
    tipsy@2: mild
    legless@5: strong
```

These keys must exist in that concept's `triggers`. An overlay replaces a named map as a whole, so patch
triggers'n their certificates coherently in the same layer. Research\-round intensity rewrites retain
matching certificates; conflicting annotations fail validation. A target grade never certifies arbitrary
source wording in `replaces`.

Automatic selection compares realised degree, independently of the soft `intensity` weighting and
`narrator_opinion`. Explicit mild or strong input needs a compatible known output. A retained modifier
can carry that degree: `very` plus an unmarked predicate is strong, while `slightly`/`a bit` is mild.
The modifier stays attached through substitution and accent/swear processing. Unsupported or conflicting
compositions stay as written; negation is retained. Clause expansions cannot silently consume a modifier.
Ordinary inputs with no stated degree retain unknown-degree options. Plans and automatic change
alternatives use the same eligibility. Dictionary discovery remains broader.

Calibration covers DRUNK and HUNGRY. Evidence'n limits are recorded in the
[alcohol degree ledger](../../research/semantic-refinement-2026-10-19/drunk-degree-calibration.md) and
[hunger degree ledger](../../research/semantic-followup-2026-10-20/hunger-degree-calibration.md).
Hunger qualifiers stay attached: `very hungry` and `slightly hungry` can remain plain when no compatible
unmarked single\-word target is available. Strong appetite can't automatically become `peckish`.
The mechanism is generic; it doesn't certify all concepts, infer missing grades from historical intensity
numbers or prove the meaning of arbitrary agent\-written prose. Similarity alone can't certify a graded
source meaning. Extending another family requires reviewed source'n target annotations.

## Noun reference and direct address

A concept's `noun_use` is `any` (default), `reference` or `address`. This distinguishes a quantified reference
such as “Everyone came” from speaking to a group in “Hi everyone”. EVERYONE takes reference; PLURAL_ADDRESS
takes address and offers plural forms such as `you mob` and `youse`. It keeps the existing noun-phrase frame.
A direct `replaces` phrase cannot bypass the concept restriction. An unknown grammatical role satisfies
neither restricted use, leaving the source wording available unchanged.

`takes_addressee: true` declares an expression that introduces a recipient, such as a greeting or thanks.
It is a boolean meaning capability, not a document setting. The reader combines that data with punctuation,
known recipient/name shapes and command grammar. An arbitrary interjection or comma does not prove address.
Simple direct addresses can transform. Ambiguous parentheticals, qualified recipients and unresolved
coordinated recipients stay as written rather than become distributive phrases. A following reference
clause with corroborated finite/governor evidence retains its separate reading. Mere absence of an address
match is not evidence of reference, and a POS guess alone cannot turn a bare command into a finite predicate.
Other noun concepts default to unrestricted use, so “Hello friend”
can still offer `mate`; YOU_PLURAL also remains usable as a subject or object.

## Context and source-English data

`genres.yaml` defines every genre policy and all three embellishment settings. Boolean switches must be
YAML booleans; guidance is text, garnish is a list of known placements or `all`, `keep_share` is a finite
number in 0–1 and `max_length` is finite and at least 1. Custom data directories provide their own policies.
The loader collects malformed genre/dialect data with the other dictionary diagnostics.

`dialect.yaml` maps `us`, `uk` and shared expressions to Australian wording. Values are text or a mapping
with `to`, optional `plural`, `frame`, `known_only` and `not_in`. Replacement/plural values are text and
`known_only` is boolean. `lint_only` flags expressions without automatic replacements. Concept
`not_in` and lexical subject-fit/POS rules keep terms of art and noun/verb senses in their own contexts.
See [translation controls](translation-controls.md) and the executable
[dialect](../../tests/functional/test_dialect.py), [noun phrase](../../tests/functional/test_noun_phrase.py)
and [schema](../../tests/functional/test_schema.py) specifications.

A concept may declare `unless_after: [for, to]` to exclude complements that do not establish its meaning.
The same restriction applies to concept triggers, an entry's direct `replaces` triggers and similarity
fallback. It reads across soft punctuation (commas and dashes), stopping at sentence, semicolon and colon
boundaries. For example, the food-appetite concept leaves “hungry for success” plain; the conservative
restriction also leaves “hungry for lunch” plain until a more specific supported construction is supplied.
The words are dictionary data, not a hunger-specific test in the engine.
Restricted meanings also stay plain when following context is unknown at an incomplete Markdown unit
edge or behind protected code. Opaque content is never read as prose to guess a complement.

## Frame vocabulary

`grammar.yaml` contains `person_nouns` (lower-case noun forms) and `adjective_nouns` (adjective to allowed
following nouns). The same adjective rule applies to attributive matches after a linking verb, so “great
disappointments” cannot evade it through a predicate frame. Multiword person triggers do not make their bare
head a person: “a party animal” does not make an animal a person. Bare person triggers and explicit role nouns
supply the person's vocabulary. Keep genuinely human singular and plural roles in the list.

Plural\-only clothin' forms remain available where they fit. Where a singular agreeing verb must remain, the
engine selects a compatible singular alternative rather than introducing “is my togs”.

Similarity fallback covers slot\-free predicate patterns with a fixed literal shape. Optional\-word patterns
remain supported by exact trigger matching; they aren't guessed through similarity.

Captured noun arguments need a nominal or supported gerund shape: “try hard cheese” and “try running
carefully” have objects, while “try hard to finish” doesn't capture “hard” as an object. A selected form
must retain captured noun/object arguments, either through its slots or identical literal wording. A
slotless variant therefore can't silently drop the tool from “try the tool”.
Short degree/nominal ambiguities such as “a bit harder” or “a little water” stay plain; the tagger alone
can't reliably settle them. Clear nominal constructions such as “a bit of cheese” remain supported.
For an unanchored terminal object slot, temporal signals distinguish “try every day” from “try every
tool”. Preposition\-headed phrases such as “at home” aren't objects. Time words used in anchored arguments,
subjects or nominal compounds remain valid: “give every day a try” and “try every day pass”. Mixed object
and time captures stay plain without trimmin' their spans. This is bounded grammar readin', not a full parse.

Local subject binding follows supported auxiliary chains'n adverbs, including progressive, perfect and
question constructions. It stops at another lexical verb or a clause boundary. This makes optional images
available for “I am feeling hungry” with the correct possessive, without changin' its auxiliary or guessing
a speaker for “feeling hungry”. Writer\-only rewrites still require a writer to preserve tense'n modality.

## Drawl comparison

Phonetic rules can declare `unless_question: true` when their grammatical placement is unsafe in a question.
The guard uses the shared sentence tokenizer, including abbreviations such as `Mr.` and `U.S.`. It applies
only to the declared rule: other grammatical question infixes remain available. Skipped matches keep their
occurrence ordinal so later seeded choices do not shift. The loader requires a real boolean.
Quoted speech can group a declaration and questions in one canonical unit; that whole unit conservatively
skips the opted-in infix. Standalone statements and imperatives remain eligible.

A literal drawl rule may declare `reads_as`, its canonical wording for lint's refrain comparison:

```yaml
- id: want-to-wanna
  match: "(?i)\\bwant to\\b"
  replace: wanna
  reads_as: want to
  prob: 0.6
  min_level: 5
```

Lint reads these annotations from the loaded dictionary, including custom data. This is a comparison spelling,
not a grammatical inverse: ambiguous `yer` is consistently read as `your`. Group-reference replacements and
spelling rules cannot declare `reads_as`. Dropped-g words are also normalised during comparison.

`grammar.yaml` may declare `name_aliases`, a mapping of exact original phrases to accepted comparison wordings.
These only affect lint fidelity, never translation. Keep them narrowly reviewed: a capitalised common phrase
such as `Christmas Trees` can have `Chrissy trees` as an alias without exempting `Christmas Island` or words
inside a person's name. Changed names without an explicit alias retain their warnings.

## Contextual images

`imagery.yaml` is optional for custom data directories. It contains a list of records with unique kebab\-case
`id`, `text`, nonempty `concepts` and `usage`. Concepts must exist in `concepts.yaml`. These include original
comparisons harvested from creative writin', not only attested traditional sayings. Entries remain the home
for reusable slang meanings, such as the `DISHONEST` sense of “as crooked as a dog's hind leg”.

| Field | Values and default |
|---|---|
| `form` | `suffix` (default, a grammatical appendage) or `rewrite` (writer must weave it in) |
| `frames` | Nonempty list of engine frames; defaults to predicate, clause and verb phrase |
| `subject` | `any` (default) or `person`, checked using the existing subject grammar |
| `unless_after` | Optional lowercase complement words; read across soft punctuation within the same clause |
| `related` | Optional reviewed related concept IDs; conditional writer suggestions only |
| `exaggeration` | 0–2, default 1; an eligibility ceiling, not a probability |
| `level` | Minimum level 1–5, default 3 |
| `tone` | `comic` (default), `grim` or `plain` |
| `origin` | `original` (default) or `familiar`; editorial provenance, not proof of attestation |
| `usage` | Required conditions and semantic boundaries for the writer |

Only `{poss}`, `{objposs}` and `{np}` slots are supported. Plans bind them only when the detection supplies
the required subject, object or noun phrase; bare lookup returns an explicitly unbound `template` card.
Unknown fields, concepts, frames, slots, invalid ranges'n duplicate IDs fail loading. Vulgarity is derived
from `swears.yaml` and can't be supplied to bypass the cap. Negative source contexts suppress meaning\-based
imagery. The matching is deterministic'n conservative, rather than full logical or discourse analysis.
See [selection and configuration](translation-controls.md#contextual-imagery) for the distinction between
writer suggestions'n automatic insertion. Historical round replays remove images referencing temporarily
set\-aside concepts in scratch only, while still rejecting genuinely unknown concepts.

## Finite clauses and sense boundaries

Question realisation supports modular subject/be/have/do clauses'n existential there/be clauses. How good is that?
have inverts directly; lexical possession takes do\-support. Fixed finite or negative clause idioms remain
available in declarations but are declined in questions when no safe modular question form exists. An outer
auxiliary such as “could” can't be left before a replacement that brings its own independent finite clause;
predicate alternatives remain available, preservin' the original auxiliary.

Ambiguous bare “establish” remains unchanged; unambiguous founding phrases retain their idioms. Restless
“turning and tossing” is held apart from throwing an object. Truthful assurance (“in all honesty”) can use
“hand on heart”, while wholehearted devotion and bare sincere/solemn manner stay distinct. These are sense
and grammar rules shared by all document presets; their tests are
[the fidelity regressions](../../tests/functional/test_fidelity_maintenance.py).

## Reviewed sense boundaries

A shared concept expresses the meaning actually established by its triggers. Physical solitude doesn't
establish emotional loneliness; a shout doesn't establish a reprimand; very little isn't exactly zero.
Named tree species, animals, baggage, package contents'n construction methods need explicit support in
the input. Compatible grammatical entries preserve source modals, object/reference slots'n location nouns
rather than silently droppin' them. These distinctions live in dictionary data'n reuse the existin'
meaning'n frame checks; optional writer imagery doesn't redefine a literal mapping.

Historical `sandy blight` remains available for casual eye-inflammation wording. Its concept declares
`not_in: [technical, official, instructions]`, honoured when those domains appear in resolved
`document_config.term_domains`. A document classifier supplies presets; no separate hidden type-specific
rule is added. Exact terms and precise protected wording keep their ordinary document-policy behaviour.

Automatic beer\-package mappings require an explicit twenty\-four\-unit amber fluid package: a 24\-pack, twenty\-four
pack, or case/carton of 24 beers. A bare case/carton may carry a different count, including in a later
qualifier, so it stays plain. The slab expression remains in the dictionary'n discoverable by lookup;
this factual boundary doesn't introduce a quantity parser.

Terminal object'n noun captures must reach a complete argument. A coordinated listener, partial multiword
name, possessive noun head or of\-qualified name stays plain when the capture can't retain it. A following
coordinated verb or fresh finite clause remains independent. The same bounded check protects speech,
scolding'n other verb constructions; it doesn't claim a full parser for arbitrary coordination.

Waltzing Matilda requires an explicitly travellin' swag carrier. Carryin' a swag alone can use the separate
baggage expression; walking country roads alone doesn't establish baggage. Exact\-zero mappings also
exclude minimising nothing\-much constructions, which may describe a small amount rather than none.
